# TWENTY YEARS HUNTING THESE WOODS. WHAT I SAW ON THE RIDGE. [color=#5C6B58]Pinned. Seen, not told.[/color]
### #1 ridge_hunter (OP) // 83.04.14 I am not a storyteller and I do not believe in ghosts. I have hunted the ridge above the valley for twenty years. I know what lives up there: the long-legged grazers we call deer because nobody bothered to name them, the burrowers, the things that click in the canopy and never come down. I have never in twenty years been afraid of the dark up there. I am writing this because I am afraid of it now.
I went up with my partner in the afternoon. At the truck, before we split up, he coughed, a bad one, he has the dust in his lungs from the processor, and he said [italic]over here, old son, give me a hand with this.[/italic] He wanted help with the tailgate. That is all. Remember it.
He felt rough after and went home early. I stayed out for the evening feed on the ridge.
### #2 ridge_hunter (OP) // 83.04.14 About an hour after dark, from down the slope, I heard him cough. The same cough. Then [italic]over here, old son, give me a hand with this.[/italic]
Same words. Same gap between the cough and the words. Same little rise on the word hand. Like a tape played back.
I nearly answered. I had my mouth open. Then I thought: he went home. I watched his truck go down the valley road. And something in the back of my head said, he is not going to say it the same way twice.
So I did not answer, and I put my lamp down the slope.
### #3 ridge_hunter (OP) // 83.04.14 Two eyes, about forty metres down, giving the light back pale, like a grazer's. But high. Much too high. Higher than my head would be if I stood on the truck.
It was standing up. Like a man stands. Very thin, I could see the ribs from where I was, and the arms hung down past its knees, and the fingers were long enough that they nearly touched the ground. The skin was pale, almost white in the lamp, like something that has been kept indoors all its life. It was breathing heavily, through the mouth, the way a dog pants.
Then it turned away from the light, and I saw its back. There were letters on it. Big ones, across the shoulders, burned in, the way a stencil is burned into a crate. I could only read the second half. YUTANI.
Then it jumped. Not ran. It went from where it was standing to the far side of the clearing in one move, maybe fifteen metres, and it did not make a sound when it landed, and it was gone.
I had my rifle in my hands the whole time. I did not lift it. I do not know why. I think I knew that if I missed, it would know exactly where I was.
### #4 mynah_theory // 83.04.15 I was the bird person in the campfire thread. I am not going to be the bird person here.
### #5 valley_skeptic // 83.04.15 YUTANI. On its back. Someone tell me again the station at the top of the valley grows mushrooms.
### #6 sap_and_saw // 83.04.16 My gran said he was a man once. A man who ate what he should not have. Something that eats people and gets taller and thinner and hungrier with each one, and talks with the voices of the people it took.
I do not want my gran to have been right.
### #7 ember_keeper (mod) // 83.04.16 ridge_hunter, thank you. Please do not go back up the ridge to look for tracks. I know you want to. I know you are a good tracker. That is exactly why it was watching you and not a grazer.
Everyone: it does not matter what it is. What matters is that it waited until it had heard a voice he trusted, and then it used it. Read the rules again.
### #8 ridge_hunter (OP) // 83.04.22 Small update. I asked my partner, very carefully, without telling him why, whether he had been up the ridge that night. He laughed and said he was flat on his back with a hot towel on his chest by eight.
I told him to stop saying [italic]old son[/italic] near the trees. He asked if I had gone soft. Maybe I have.
### #9 old_son // 83.05.09 He told me. I read the thread. I made him show me.
I did not say those words near the trees again. Last night something stood at the edge of the clearing behind our hab and said them anyway, in my voice, with my cough, over and over, for an hour. It has learned them now. It does not need me any more.
We have moved into town.
